---
title: "Troubleshooting"
description: "Symptom-by-symptom fixes for hooks that don't fire, fire wrong, or fire twice."
---

A hook misbehaved. captain-hook ships no `doctor` command. You diagnose with two tools, the dispatch logs and a re-run of your inline tests.

## Diagnostic commands

Reach for these first. The logs show what dispatch actually saw; the tests show what your conditions match.

```bash
uvx capt-hook logs                          # Print the most recent session's log
uvx capt-hook logs --tail 40                # Show only the last 40 lines
uvx capt-hook logs --session <id-or-path>   # Target a specific session (id, or transcript path)
uvx capt-hook --hooks <dir> test            # Re-run inline tests; prints the Input and PASS/FAIL
uvx capt-hook --hooks <dir> test --json     # One record per test: id, status, expected, reason
```

`logs` reads from the log directory, which defaults to `~/.cache/captain-hook/logs`. Each session writes one log file there. To target a past session, pass its id, or pass the transcript path and `logs` hashes it for you. See [Configuration](packs.qmd#log_dir) to relocate the directory.

If a hook never appears in the log, dispatch never reached it. Work through [It never fires](#it-never-fires).

## Confirm the hook fires

Confirm three things, in order.

First, re-run the inline tests.

```bash
uvx capt-hook --hooks <dir> test
```

Each test prints the `Input` it built and a PASS or FAIL. A FAIL means your conditions don't match the input you expect, so fix the condition before you touch dispatch. If the test passes but the hook still seems dead, move on.

Second, check that `--hooks` points at the directory holding your hook file. captain-hook loads `.py` files under that root and nothing else.

Third, read the session log.

```bash
uvx capt-hook logs --tail 40
```

A firing hook leaves a dispatch line here. If you see the event arrive but no line for your hook, a condition skipped it. If you see no event at all, the hook targets the wrong event or the captain-hook plugin isn't enabled in this session.

## It fires too often

A hook that fires on every event, or twice per event, is matching too broadly. Tighten it three ways.

Narrow the conditions. Add a `skip_if` for the cases you want to spare, or a tighter `only_if` glob. A `FilePath("**/*.py")` matches every Python file in the project; `FilePath("src/**/*.py")` matches only your source tree. See the [conditions cheatsheet](../reference/conditions.qmd) for every condition and the [conditions guide](primitives.qmd#filter-with-conditions) for how to combine them.

Cap the count. A `nudge` already defaults to one fire, or three when signal-scored, and budgets count per agent context — the main agent and each subagent get their own allowance; pass `max_fires=N` to change the cap. The LLM primitives also default low, with `llm_gate` at 1 and `llm_nudge` at 3. See the [primitives reference](../reference/primitives.qmd).

Check the event set. A hook registered with `Event.Stop | Event.SubagentStop` fires on both. Confirm that both belong by reading the [events reference](../reference/events.qmd).

## It never fires

The hook is silent because dispatch never matched it. Check four causes.

Wrong event. Each primitive picks a default event. `block_command` and a bare `nudge` target `PreToolUse`, a signal-scored `nudge` targets `PostToolUse`, and a blocking `gate` targets `Event.Stop | Event.SubagentStop`. If you need a different one, pass `events=` explicitly. The [events reference](../reference/events.qmd) lists which event fires when.

Unsatisfiable conditions. An `only_if` is AND, so every condition must match at once. A hook with `only_if=[Tool("Bash"), FilePath("**/*.py")]` never fires, because a Bash command carries no file path. Run `uvx capt-hook --hooks <dir> test` and read the `Input` each test built against your conditions.

Plugin not enabled. The captain-hook plugin registers every hook event; without it, no event reaches dispatch at all. Confirm `.claude/settings.json` still enables `captain-hook`, and re-run `uvx capt-hook init` if the registration is missing.

Session not fresh. Claude Code loads plugin hooks at session start. A hook on a brand-new event, or a just-enabled plugin, takes effect when the next session starts.

## The signed host is missing or dispatch fails

Every event runs the plugin's `bin/hook`, which binrun resolves to the `capt-hookd` inside
`~/Applications/Captain Hook.app`. If the app is missing or older than the plugin needs, dispatch exits non-zero
instead of falling back to an unfenced wheel. A `PreToolUse` or `PermissionRequest` that names a
session-ending program instead runs under your permissions with a skip note and exit 0.
Install or repair the application:

```bash
uvx capt-hook helper install
```

The wheel that handles each event is chosen by the app itself: the host runs the `capt-hook`
wheel at exactly its own build, so the wheel and app cannot drift apart. The app also keeps itself current — a
session-start check, at most one per 12 hours, upgrades the formula in the background and posts a
notification when the upgrade lands ([how it works](how-it-works.qmd#the-host-keeps-itself-current)).
The manual path still works — check what's installed, upgrade the Cellar, then deploy from it:

```bash
"$HOME/Applications/Captain Hook.app/Contents/Helpers/capt-hookd" version
brew upgrade --formula yasyf/tap/captain-hook
uvx capt-hook helper install
```

Legacy dispatch entries. The only consumer command is `"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/hook" run <Event>` from the
captain-hook plugin. A surviving `uvx --isolated --from capt-hook hook run
<Event>` line — an old plugin release, or a hand-copied settings entry — is a second registration: Claude Code dedupes hook commands per registering source, not
globally, so every hook on that event can run twice. The tell is doubled output: two permission
prompts for one tool call, the same block message landing twice, or a side-effecting hook
applying its effect twice. Update the plugin and delete hand-wired entries from project settings;
do not preserve them as a fallback:

```
/plugin marketplace update captain-hook
/plugin update
```

A session that is already running keeps the old hook commands until you run `/reload-plugins` or
start a new session. Sessions on plugin 12.28 or older fail every hook until they reload.

## Quiet every hook for a while

Pause every captain-hook hook across all sessions, guards included. This needs the signed host
from this release; [update the host](#the-signed-host-is-missing-or-dispatch-fails) first.
Set a pause, check its status, or lift it early:

```bash
uvx capt-hook pause --for 30m --reason "desktop CPU saturation"
uvx capt-hook pause --status
uvx capt-hook resume
```

The reason is optional. Durations such as `45s`, `30m`, and `1h` work; the cap is one hour.
The pause expires by itself, with no cleanup. Every event returns without dispatch, whichever
plugin version the session is pinned to, and a `SessionStart` banner names the expiry and how to
resume. Guards are off for the whole pause.

The command writes `pause.json` under `$CAPTAIN_HOOK_STATE_DIR` (default `~/.claude/state`).
A malformed file or an expiry more than an hour away leaves hooks running.

Quiet hooks only through `uvx capt-hook pause`; never edit the plugin cache. An edited `bin/hook`
can silence every hook in every session pinned to that version with no signal, while Claude Code
still prints `completed successfully`.

## Check a restored plugin launcher

A `captain-hook fault: plugin launcher` warning naming `LauncherTampered` means captain-hook
found a changed `bin/hook` and restored what that version shipped in git, including its mode and
whether it was a symlink. The warning lists the restored versions.

`SessionStart` checks installed versions and versions still in use by a live process, after replying
and at most once per ten minutes. A repair appears in the next `SessionStart` warning. Look for the
`launcher restored:` line in `~/.claude/state/update/update.log`, or
`$CAPTAIN_HOOK_STATE_DIR/update/update.log` when you override the state directory.

Run the check and repair by hand:

```bash
uvx capt-hook update launchers
```

## A SessionStart warning about `pack attach`

Claude Code shows a non-blocking hook warning at session start naming a failed `capt-hook pack attach` command. An enabled plugin still ships the attach line from the pre-10.0.0 contract; the command no longer exists, so the hook exits non-zero and Claude Code reports it. The warning is not the real problem: a plugin that old also predates the fixed `capt-hook/` layout, so its pack no longer loads at all — `uvx capt-hook pack list` shows no `plugin` row for it. Both symptoms clear when the plugin ships a release on the current contract; [Ship a pack in a Claude plugin](packs.qmd#ship-a-pack-in-a-plugin) covers the layout.

## A plugin lands disabled with `dependency-unsatisfied`

A pack plugin declares captain-hook as a `plugin.json` dependency, and Claude Code won't add an unknown marketplace from a dependency alone — so on a machine that has never seen captain-hook, the plugin installs but lands disabled. Register the marketplace once and the dependency resolves:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add yasyf/captain-hook
```

`capt-hook init` in any repo does the same as a side effect. See [Tell users how to install](packs.qmd#tell-users-how-to-install).

## `NlpSignal` hooks need the spaCy model {#nlpsignal-hooks-need-the-spacy-model}

Hooks that use `NlpSignal` need the `en_core_web_sm` spaCy model (~13 MB). A pack that declares it under `resources` in its descriptor, as `general` and `steering` do, provisions it eagerly: `init` downloads it on the spot, and an async `SessionStart` hook re-checks at every session start, so an install that deferred the download (offline, say) heals itself the next session. A live hook never downloads the spaCy model; that would be a silent network fetch behind the agent's back, so it raises a `RuntimeError` with an install hint instead.

Only `Phrase.expand` reads the `oewn:2025` WordNet lexicon, a 13 MB download that imports into a 113 MB database. No builtin pack calls it, so a session that runs only builtin hooks never touches WordNet. The first hook that reads an expanded phrase provisions the lexicon and waits for it. One process imports into a staging copy while every other session and thread waits on the same file lock, and the database moves into place only after the import finishes and passes an integrity check. A stamp beside the database records that, and a database no stamp vouches for is rebuilt, never read. That covers a database an interrupted run left behind, one that changed since its stamp, and one an earlier capt-hook version imported in place. To pay for the import at session start instead of inside a hook, declare `wordnet:oewn:2025` under `resources` in the pack's descriptor.

A hook that raises `RuntimeError: spaCy model 'en_core_web_sm' is not installed` means provisioning never ran for this project. Re-run `init`; it downloads every declared resource on the spot, and the async `SessionStart` hook re-checks at every session start after that.

```bash
uvx capt-hook init
```

A standalone hooks directory that uses NLP outside any pack skips eager provisioning. Provision the resources directly with the bundled helper.

```bash
python -c "from captain_hook.util.model_cache import ensure_nlp_resources; ensure_nlp_resources()"
```

## Case study, a block that caught a safe command

You add a hook that blocks `git stash`, because your team uses `jj` instead.

```python
from captain_hook import hook, Event, Runs, Tool

hook(
    Event.PreToolUse,
    message="Use jj shelve instead of git stash",
    block=True,
    only_if=[Tool("Bash"), Runs("git", "stash")],
)
```

The block works. It also blocks `git stash pop`, because `Runs` matches an argv *prefix* and `["git", "stash", "pop"]` starts with `["git", "stash"]`. Popping a stash is safe, so the hook now blocks a command you want to allow.

Fix it with a `skip_if`, which skips the hook when any of its conditions match. List the safe subcommands there, each as its own argv prefix.

```python
from captain_hook import Or

hook(
    Event.PreToolUse,
    message="Use jj shelve instead of git stash",
    block=True,
    only_if=[Tool("Bash"), Runs("git", "stash")],
    skip_if=[
        Or(
            Runs("git", "stash", "pop"),
            Runs("git", "stash", "apply"),
            Runs("git", "stash", "list"),
            Runs("git", "stash", "show"),
        )
    ],
)
```

Now the safe subcommands pass through while a bare `git stash` still blocks. A re-run of `uvx capt-hook --hooks <dir> test` with a test for each subcommand confirms the split.

Write the exemption structurally, the way the block itself is written. A regex `skip_if` on a blocking hook fails in the direction nobody notices: `Command(r"git\s+stash\s+(pop|apply|list|show)")` also matches `echo "git stash pop"`, and an exemption that is too wide stands the block down without saying so. `Runs` compares tokens, so the exemption covers the four commands it names and nothing else.
